sentences.text: On 2 August 2027 the Moon passes exactly between the Sun and the Earth, and this time it covers the Sun completely.
Because it is in the part of its orbit close to Earth, it looks eight per cent larger than the Sun in the sky, and its full shadow draws a wide band.

Let's turn back to look at Earth: the Moon's shadow travels as a dark spot across the day side, from the Atlantic to the Strait of Gibraltar, along North Africa to Egypt, then over the Red Sea to Arabia and Somalia.
The longest totality is near Luxor: for six minutes and twenty-three seconds the daytime sky goes dark and the Sun's crown, the corona, is visible to the naked eye.
Europe, the Middle East and Turkey see a partial eclipse; never look at the Sun without eclipse glasses.
